scope.flow: AtomWallet UserOperation signature validation via EntryPoint
scope.environment: ERC-4337 Account Abstraction; AtomWallet, Bundler, EntryPoint
evidence: the time validation of UserOperation in `AtomWallet` can be bypassed/manipulated

`AtomWallet` is an ERC-4337 compliant Account Abstraction wallet. The owner of the `AtomWallet` can sign  UserOperation and send it to a Bundler. The Bundler will verify the UserOperation and execute it on sender's behalf through `EntryPoint`.

When verifying the signature of `UserOperation`, `EntryPoint` will check returned `validAfter` and `validUntil`. The `UserOperation` can not be executed if the valid period is expired. The following is the calling process in [`EntryPoint`](https://github.com/eth-infinitism/account-abstraction/blob/cc3893bcaf2272c163ce89d5eb9eadb8e6b52db7/contracts/core/EntryPoint.sol#L58-L76):
**The `validationData` is returned from [`AtomWallet#_validateSignature()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2026-03-intuition/blob/main/src/protocol/wallet/AtomWallet.sol#L285-L311)**:

However, Both `validUntil` and `validAfter` can be manipulated, the AtomWallet fails to enforce validUntil and validAfter constraints, permitting the execution of UserOperations outside of their intended validity period.
The root cause is that `validUntil` and `validAfter` are excluded from the UserOperation signature hash. Consequently, these values can be modified without invalidating the signature.
